:::{#thm-residual-variance-more-covariates}
#### A further covariate cannot raise the average residual variance

Let $\Predvar$ and $Z$ be [covariates](#def-covariate) of one observation from a [population](exploratory-descriptive.qmd#def-population),
and let $\Outvar$ be its outcome, with $\E{\Outvar^2} < \infty$.

The [residual variance](#def-irreducible-error) of $\Outvar$ given $\Predvar$ and $Z$, averaged over the covariate values,
is at most the residual variance given $\Predvar$ alone, averaged in the same way:

$$
\E{\Var{\Outvar \mid \Predvar, Z}} \le \E{\Var{\Outvar \mid \Predvar}}.
$$ {#eq-residual-variance-more-covariates}

:::

::: proof
@exr-residual-variance-more-covariates splits the average residual variance given $\Predvar$ into two terms.
The second term is the expectation of a [variance](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#def-variance), which is never negative.

$$
\ba
\E{\Var{\Outvar \mid \Predvar}}
&= \E{\Var{\Outvar \mid \Predvar, Z}} + \E{\Var{\E{\Outvar \mid \Predvar, Z} \mid \Predvar}}
&& \text{(the split of the exercise)} \\
&\ge \E{\Var{\Outvar \mid \Predvar, Z}} + 0
&& \text{(a variance is nonnegative, so its expectation is too)} \\
&= \E{\Var{\Outvar \mid \Predvar, Z}}
&& \text{(} a + 0 = a \text{)}
\ea
$$

:::
